sections.overview: The spotted flycatcher is a small, grey-brown, long-winged songbird that hunts flying insects from a perch. It is one of the latest summer visitors to Britain and winters in Africa, and its numbers there have collapsed over decades.
sections.identification: About the size of a robin, an adult weighs roughly 14.5 g and has a wing length near 86 mm. The back, head, wings and tail are grey-brown and the underparts pale buff with brown streaking on the breast; the name is a misnomer, as it is more streaked than spotted. The sexes look alike; juveniles are spotty and greyer.
sections.habitat: It lives in woodland, mature gardens and parks with many trees, and in mature hedgerows with trees on farmland. In Britain and Ireland it breeds throughout except in the far north and west.
sections.diet: It eats flying insects such as flies, butterflies, wasps and craneflies. It watches from a high perch, darts out to catch one in the air, and often returns to the same spot.
sections.behavior: It typically arrives in late April or May and leaves in September. Birds tracked by BTO researchers have wintered as far south as Namibia, some 7,000 km from their breeding site. The call is a repetitive, high-pitched tzee and the song a series of scratchy warbles.
sections.reproduction: The open cup nest is placed on ledges in and around buildings or on creepers against walls and trees. In Britain the first clutch averages 6 June, with typically two broods of four or five eggs. The female alone incubates for 13–14 days and the chicks fledge after about 13–16 days. Breeding typically starts at one year.
sections.ecology: Birds, especially jays, cause most nest predation: in a nest-camera study they accounted for 17 of 20 events. Nests in gardens fledged about twice as many chicks as those in woodland or farmland. A typical adult lives about two years; the oldest ringed bird reached eight.
sections.conservation: The IUCN Red List classes it as Least Concern, but in the UK it is Red-listed. The breeding population was about 42,000 territories in 2016 and fell by 92% between 1967 and 2024; it has also declined across Europe since 1980. Falling first-year survival seems the main driver, but the ecological cause remains uncertain.
